items.title: Breakfast television
items.line: BBC Breakfast Time started in January 1983 and ITV's TV-am followed on 1 February, two weeks later, brought forward from June so the BBC wouldn't have the mornings to itself.

items.title: Motorola DynaTAC
items.line: Unveiled on 6 March 1983, the first handheld mobile phone you could buy.

items.title: Top of the Pops 1,000
items.line: The BBC chart show reached its thousandth episode in 1983. Spandau Ballet held number one with 'True' for a fourth week and closed it, beside a giant birthday cake.

items.title: Return of the Jedi
items.line: Released on 25 May 1983 and the biggest film of the year, taking $374 million worldwide on its first run. It was filmed in England, California and Arizona.

items.title: Thatcher's landslide
items.line: At the general election on 9 June 1983 the Conservatives won a majority of 144, the most decisive result since 1945, on the back of the Falklands and a returning economy.

items.title: Brink's-Mat robbery
items.line: On 26 November 1983 six men broke into a warehouse near Heathrow and left with £26 million in gold bullion, diamonds and cash. Most of the gold was never found.

items.title: The M*A*S*H finale
items.line: 'Goodbye, Farewell and Amen' aired on CBS on 28 February 1983 to 105.97 million US viewers. It was the most-watched broadcast in American history until the Super Bowl in February 2010.

items.title: Motown 25 and the moonwalk
items.line: Taped at the Pasadena Civic Auditorium on 25 March 1983 and shown on NBC on 16 May, Motown 25 had Michael Jackson mime 'Billie Jean' and do the moonwalk on TV for the first time.

items.title: Flashdance
items.line: Flashdance opened on 15 April 1983, cost $7 million and took about $201.5 million. MTV ran its dance scenes as free videos, and Irene Cara's 'What a Feeling' went to number 1 in May.

items.title: Sally Ride
items.line: On 18 June 1983 Sally Ride flew on Challenger's STS-7 mission, the first American woman in space. She was 32.

items.title: Nintendo Famicom
items.line: Nintendo launched the Famicom in Japan on 15 July 1983 at ¥14,800 with Donkey Kong, Donkey Kong Jr. and Popeye. The US got it as the NES in a New York test market in October 1985.

items.title: Yamaha DX7
items.line: Yamaha's DX7 came out in 1983 at $1,995. By 1986 its 'E Piano 1' preset was on 40 percent of the Hot 100 number ones, and some players dropped the Rhodes for it.
